issues.description: Script sends requests to third-party APIs (SponsorBlock and multiple Cobalt instances) using GM_xmlhttpRequest. These requests include the current YouTube video ID, which may be considered user activity data.
issues.location: CFG.sbApi, CFG.cobaltInstances, SponsorBlock and download logic
issues.recommendation: Clearly inform users about data transmission. Consider proxying requests or minimizing data sent if privacy is a concern.

issues.description: Script stores and retrieves user settings (ad, sponsorblock, quality toggles) using GM_setValue/GM_getValue. No sensitive data (like cookies or passwords) is accessed.
issues.location: Persistent state section (S object, save function)
issues.recommendation: No action needed unless sensitive data is stored in the future.

issues.description: The script requests GM_xmlhttpRequest permission, which is necessary for cross-origin API calls, but does not request unnecessary high-privilege grants.
issues.recommendation: Maintain least privilege. No excessive permissions detected.

issues.description: All third-party endpoints are hardcoded and well-known (SponsorBlock and Cobalt public instances). No dynamic code loading or @require from untrusted sources.
issues.recommendation: Continue to monitor the trustworthiness of these endpoints.

script_name: EasyTube V3 — Ad Skip, SponsorBlock & HD Download⬇️🚀
summary: The script transmits YouTube video IDs to third-party APIs (SponsorBlock and Cobalt downloaders) to provide its core features. No evidence of sensitive data (cookies, credentials, clipboard, or keylogging) collection or transmission. No code obfuscation, remote code execution, or DOM XSS risks detected. Permissions are appropriate for the functionality. Supply chain risk is moderate due to reliance on public Cobalt instances. Overall, the script is safe for most users, but privacy-conscious users should be aware of the data sent to external services.
